narr: Tropical Storm Chantal made landfall over northeastern South Carolina during the morning hours of July 6. The remnants of Chantal then tracked west-northwest into portions of central North Carolina, stalling out over the area before tracking east-northeast into Virginia by the 7th of July. Catastrophic flash flooding occurred from record rainfall of up to 11 inches in some spots of the Piedmont, included 6 flash flood fatalities across Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Widespread flooding particularly affected the counties of Orange, Chatman, and Moore. Four EF-1 tornadoes also touched down over portions Lee, Chatham, Alamance, and Orange Counties. Preliminary loss estimates across central North Carolina exceeded 40 million.
ev: Aberdeen Creek flooded parts of North Carolina Highway 5 and US Highway 1 with several roads closed in the area. Damage estimates may have exceeded 5 million, including to roads, bridges, infrastructure, and residential areas.
High water was reported across both lanes of traffic on Farm Life School Road.
Flooding was reported along Juniper Lake Road near Highway 15-501.
Several roads were flooded in southern Person County, with multiple roads closed.
US Highway 158 was closed in both directions near Hyco Creek Farm Road due to flooding along South Hyco Creek.
Hester Store Road was closed in both directions near Robert Hester Road due to flooding along Mill Creek.
Tom Bowes Road was closed in both directions near Whitefield Farm Road due to flooding of the nearby creek crossing.
North Turnpike road was closed due to flooding.
Norton Road was flooded and closed due to flood waters.
There were several reports of flash flooding and flooded roads across northern Durham.
The left lane of Interstate 40 was closed from Exit 150 at Jimmie Kerr Road to Exit 153 at Trollingwood Hawfields Road due to flooding.

Deputies responded to a report of a missing period last seen driving near Jones Drive and Calloway Drive. The body of a man was later recovered in a creek downstream. Another man was found dead also due to flooding. Both fatalities were the result of swift high water across the roadway.
Oakwood Drive north of Pittsboro was flooded due to heavy rainfall.
Two boaters launched a canoe from Marthas Chapel Road in the early evening hours. One body was found the morning of the 8th, and another found the morning of the 9th of July.
Both lanes of Highway 902 just west of Chatham Central High School were washed out due to flooding. Nearly twenty feet of roadway had been washed away.
Over 80 roads across the county were flooded, with multiple stalled cars, and nearly 33 water rescues across Chatham County, including one at the location near Siler City.
North Carolina highway 87 was impassable where it crossed Terrels Creek, near Chicken Bridge Road, and where it crossed Long Branch Creek, near Castle Rock Farm Road.
One person died when their car traveling on Farrington Point Road entered floodwaters. The driver was swept away.
Flooding was reported along portions of Interstate 85/40. The Eastbound lanes were closed near Buckhorn Road.
The vehicle of a 58 year old female on her way to work was submerged in flood waters. The victim was swept away upon trying to exit the vehicle.

There were numerous reports of stranded/submerged vehicles, washed out roadways, apartments and residential homes flooded, and law enforcement performed multiple water rescues, including one at Camelot Village. Total estimated damages may have exceeded 30 million across Orange County.
Houses were flooded with stranded vehicles reported near Route 501 and South Elliott Road.
Mail trucks were submerged in Chapel Hill near South Estes drive and Willow Drive.
One lane was closed along Interstate 85 due to flooding near exit 165.
Erwin Road was closed due to flooding.
Buckhorn Road was closed due to flooding near exit 157 of Interstate 40.
The public reported an impassable roadway with rapidly-flowing water covering US 15-501 in Southern Pines.
At least thirteen water rescues were reported across Moore County.
